clue.text: Space for change bowler given second over from the other end

indicators.note: change is an imperative here, telling the solver to alter the order of the letters of bowler
read from the other end means the pieces before it are written backwards

parts.note: MO is short for moment, a second
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A captain needs room to swap in a new bowler before the second over from the far end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' makes ELBOWR from BOWLER; 'from the other end' turns MO + O into OOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Elbow room is a common idiom for enough space to move about freely.

clue.text: Correspondence taken up in Parliament

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means the letters are read upwards, so backwards
in tells us the answer sits inside the word Parliament

explanation.surface: Letters received are being raised in a parliamentary debate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to LIAME inside parLIAMEnt; 'taken up' turns it round in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Email is electronic correspondence, the modern form of written messages.

clue.text: This 'title' could be 'tile'

parts.note: the quoted word is the result: the answer read as an instruction (bar, meaning except) acts on the word title to leave this

explanation.surface: A wordplay joke: drop a letter from one word and you have another.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: BAR ONE T, with bar meaning 'except', is what turns 'title' into 'tile'.
explanation.definitionFit: A baronet holds a hereditary British rank, so the word names a title of nobility.

clue.text: Desire, but with little morality

parts.note: to want is to desire
but and only both mean merely, as in 'but a child'

explanation.surface: Lust described as craving with scant regard for ethics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' in its old sense 'merely' gives ONLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting wantonly is behaving in a loose, unrestrained or immoral way.

clue.text: See 3
Thirteen Enigma Variations Elgar originally pictured within Nimrod puzzled composer

indicators.note: pictured within puts one set of letters inside the other, as a picture inside a frame
puzzled suggests the letters of Nimrod are jumbled
originally takes the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: Elgar's Enigma Variations, which includes the famous Nimrod, set as a puzzle about another composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Nimrod really is one of Elgar's Enigma Variations, which makes the clue read like a music note; 'puzzled' rearranges NIMROD and 'pictured within' sets TEVE inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Claudio Monteverdi was the Italian composer of the opera L'Orfeo.

clue.text: Where Epicurus came from when rejecting spicy snacks?

indicators.note: rejecting means the following word is thrown out of the snacks

parts.note: samosas are spicy fried pastries
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A philosopher of pleasure turning down spicy snacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' takes AS out of SAMOSAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek philosopher Epicurus was born on the Aegean island of Samos.

clue.text: Not, say, spaghetti hoops on a round of toast?

definitions.text: Not, say, spaghetti hoops on a round of toast?

parts.words: Not, say, spaghetti hoops on a round of toast?
parts.note: a meal made of circles on a circle is round, so jokingly it is not the opposite shape

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on tinned pasta on toast as a proper dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: Hoops on a round slice are all circles, so this is not the opposite-shaped meal: a substantial, filling one.
explanation.definitionFit: A square meal is an idiom for a substantial, nourishing feed.

clue.text: Spooner's swimmer might seize the chance

indicators.note: Spooner's tells us to swap the opening sounds of the two words, as Reverend Spooner did

parts.note: a hake is a fish, so a swimmer
may and might are both verbs of possibility

explanation.surface: A swimmer seizing an opportunity.
explanation.walkthrough: HAKE MAY with H and M swapped gives MAKE HAY.
explanation.definitionFit: To make hay (while the sun shines) is an idiom for taking advantage of an opportunity.

clue.text: Kentish Town station's entrance surveyed by female eagles

indicators.note: in a down clue, being surveyed by means sitting below the pieces that look down on it

parts.note: she is the female pronoun
ernes are sea eagles, a crossword favourite

indicators.note: the entrance of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The entrance of Kentish Town station, a London stop, watched by female birds of prey.
explanation.walkthrough: Kentish Town is a London district, but here it means a town in Kent: Sheerness, on the Isle of Sheppey.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheerness is a port town in the county of Kent, so it is literally a Kentish town.

clue.text: One injured ankle in thrills?

parts.note: a means one, as in 'a dozen'

indicators.note: thrills suggests the letters are stirred up and set quivering into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who hurt their ankle chasing excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrills' shuffles INJURED ANKLE IN into DRENALINJUNKIE after A. The whole clue also describes the answer: a thrill-seeker who hurts an ankle doing it.
explanation.definitionFit: An adrenalin junkie craves dangerous excitement, the sort that leads to sprained ankles.

clue.text: Man in field badly wants a pee

parts.note: longs to means wants badly
P is how pee, the letter or penny, is written

explanation.surface: A cricketer out in the field is desperate for the toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: LONG STOP is a cricket fielding position behind the wicketkeeper near the boundary. 'pee' sounds like the letter P.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, the long stop is a fielder, so the answer is a man in the field.

clue.text: Brand the Goddess of Pop 'a looker'?

parts.note: to brand an animal is to sear it with a hot iron
Cher is the singer nicknamed the Goddess of Pop

explanation.surface: Calling a pop diva good-looking, with branding as in marketing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looker' usually means an attractive person, which fits Cher; here it is literal, one who looks.
explanation.definitionFit: A searcher is someone who looks for something, so literally one who looks.

clue.text: As bespoke tailor did?

parts.note: a tailor making a made-to-order suit first takes the client's measurements

explanation.surface: What a tailor of made-to-order clothes did.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase also means 'proved good enough', the sense the solver must reach through the tailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a client's measurements is literally what this phrase describes, and it also means proving adequate.

clue.text: Dressing paper boy in bag in the van

indicators.note: in the van means at the front, so the bag piece leads the paper
in places the boy inside the bag

parts.note: a sac is a bag-like part of an animal or plant
lad means boy
a ream is a quantity of paper

explanation.surface: A paper boy is putting on a dressing, or sitting in a bag in a delivery van.
explanation.walkthrough: SALAD CREAM is a tangy British mayonnaise-like condiment. 'in the van' means leading: SALADC goes before REAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Salad cream is a dressing for salads, popular in Britain.

clue.text: A sea chest, possibly? Possibly, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of a sea chest might be arranged another way

parts.note: maybe means possibly

explanation.surface: A nervous guess about a seafarer's trunk, repeated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' (the first) rearranges A SEA CHEST into AS THE CASE.
explanation.definitionFit: As the case may be is an idiom meaning according to circumstances, whichever applies.

clue.text: As Fellini said to directors, 'Quickly, get on!'

parts.note: alla is Italian for 'in the style of', so the Italian director Fellini would say it for as
a company's directors make up its board

explanation.surface: A film director urging his crew to hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: Fellini is the Italian film director, so 'as' is said in Italian; 'directors' is a company board, not film-makers.
explanation.definitionFit: All aboard is the call telling passengers to get on a vehicle quickly before it leaves.

clue.text: See 14
Lamb Chop-Orville double act from this pair's island?

parts.note: Lamb Chop was the sock puppet of ventriloquist Shari Lewis
a double act is two people together, the joining word and
Orville the duck was the puppet of ventriloquist Keith Harris

explanation.surface: Two ventriloquist puppets form a pair whose names suggest a place.
explanation.walkthrough: Shari Lewis and Keith Harris were ventriloquists famous on TV for Lamb Chop and Orville.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis and Harris is the largest island of the Outer Hebrides, off Scotland.

clue.text: Dangerous customer and what he's disguised as something transitional?

parts.note: a wolf is a predator, a dangerous type
the wolf in sheep's clothing is disguised as a ram

explanation.surface: A shady character and his disguise, as in a wolf in sheep's clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transitional' points to the transition metals of the periodic table.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolfram is tungsten, a transition metal in the periodic table.

clue.text: See 16
This wine would struggle to be nastier

indicators.note: struggle suggests the letters of nastier wrestle into a new order

explanation.surface: A wine that would have trouble being any worse.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards in sense: the answer's letters, if they struggled, would make NASTIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: With obvious strain one bears warrior's sword

parts.note: bald means plain or obvious, as in a bald statement
a rick is a sprain or strain

explanation.surface: Someone straining visibly to carry a warrior's heavy sword.
explanation.walkthrough: Baldrick is a variant spelling of baldric; Baldrick is also the servant in Blackadder.
explanation.definitionFit: A baldric is a belt slung over the shoulder to carry a sword.

clue.text: See 10
Opt for a grape?

parts.note: the clue word is the output of the wordplay: the answer, split up and read as an instruction, would build this word

explanation.surface: Choosing a particular grape.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: PINOT read as 'P in OT' builds OPT.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinot is a family of grape varieties, such as pinot noir.

clue.text: Like 11's visionary feature of colonnade?

parts.note: the answer to 11 contains a visionary, a seer, whose letters wrap round a colonnade feature; the answer describes that layout

explanation.surface: A seer's vision of the arches of a colonnade.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 is SEARCHER: SEER (visionary) placed over ARCH. Overarch describes that and also what a colonnade's arches do.
explanation.definitionFit: Arches overarch a colonnade, spanning the space between columns.

clue.text: See 23
Possible reason we can't cross the river here? One's left work, in short

indicators.note: has left means it has gone, so the letter is removed

parts.words: Possible reason we can't cross the river here?
parts.note: a bridge diversion would stop traffic crossing the river
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A road sign explaining why the river crossing is closed.
explanation.walkthrough: ''s left' drops I from A BRIDGE DIVERSION.
explanation.definitionFit: An abridged version is a shortened edition of a written work.

clue.text: Stop dead: cougar to the left

indicators.note: going to the left means reading right to left, backwards

parts.note: cougar and puma are names for the same big cat

explanation.surface: A cougar suddenly halts and turns away to the left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the left' turns D + PUMA round.
explanation.definitionFit: To dam up a river is to block it, bringing the flow to a stop.

clue.text: Longing for England, Browning now reviewed parade?

definitions.text: Longing for England, Browning now reviewed
definitions.meaning: Browning's poem of longing begins 'Oh, to be in England now that April's there', so the month before has gone
a ceremonial parade before a reviewing officer

explanation.surface: A poet's homesickness for England, and a military review.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Browning's 'Home-Thoughts, from Abroad' longs for England 'now that April's there': March is past. 'reviewed' also fits troops reviewed at a parade.
explanation.definitionFit: A march past is a procession of troops saluting a dignitary.
